items.target: P06-B6a + P06-B6b (Prov.14.26 / Prov.14.27 single_proverb singles, demotion of retired P06-075)
items.evidence: Spans/unit_type/parent_collection match boss B-6 spec exactly (Prov.14.26-Prov.14.26 and Prov.14.27-Prov.14.27, both single_proverb, C2). Construct-phrase facts re-derived and byte-true: 14:26 opens bet-prefixed adverbial בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה with following subject מִבְטַח עֹ֑ז; 14:27 opens bare subject יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה with predicate מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים -- both confirmed byte-identical against verse_map_oshb.json. Fear-of-Yahweh digit decomposition re-derived token-by-token from consonantal_index.json: contiguous substring יראת יהוה = 15 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel exact match); decomposed as bare word-bound יראת = 10 verses (1.7, 2.5, 8.13, 9.10, 10.27, 14.27, 15.33, 19.23, 22.4, 31.30) and prefixed hosts = 5 verses (ויראת 1.29, ביראת 14.26/15.16/23.17, וביראת 16.6) -- exact match to both rows' claims, and neither sub-set contains an adjacent pair (verified). 13:14 tail-identity confirmed: מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת is byte-identical at 13:14 and 14:27 (sweep=2), and מקור חיים = 4 verses (10.11, 13.14, 14.27, 16.22) -- both exact. check_tiling.py over Prov.14.1-Prov.14.35 = GREEN (0 gaps/overlaps), P06-074 ending 14:25 and P06-076 opening 14:28 as specced. citation_sweep.py, check_refs_mirror.py, check_marks.py all GREEN on the pair. Downstream row P06-041 (13:14) correctly cites the 14:27 tie with matching digits; no stale reference to retired id P06-075 anywhere in rows_v1.jsonl. DEFECT: check_universals.py FLAGS both rows (non-GREEN) on the phrase 'the verse states one continuous benefit-clause' (observed_substrate_signals) -- 'continuous' is in the tool's flagged lexicon and has no adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation in the same sentence. This is a literal miss against B-6's own named cure test #5 ('check_universals.py ... GREEN on both new rows'), reproduced when the tool is scoped to just these two rows (status FLAGS, not GREEN). Content-wise this reads as a heuristic false positive -- the sentence describes the verse's own internal grammatical unity, not a corpus-wide exclusivity claim -- and the tool's own docstring calls such hits 'candidates for review, not auto-fails,' but the named tool-status gate is not literally satisfied as written.
